tdout": "> ## Documentation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.mcpjam.com/llms.txt\n> Use this file
to discover all available pages before exploring further.\n# MCPJam API\n> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam p

rojects: diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.
> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview
.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change, including in\n>
breaking ways, while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n>
reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z
) or\n> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).\n> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-ke

ys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right
back on the API keys page.\nThe MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your\n[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hoste

d/overview.md) projects (from CI, scripts, or your own agents)
without opening the UI.
What you can do with it today:
* **Disco
ver your resources**: list your projects, their servers, eval\n suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is\n
self-serve\n* **Validate a server**: connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot\n* **Run the doctor**: the probe → c
onnect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements**: does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools
, prompts, and resources**: the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt**: execute primitives and get the MCP r
esult back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot**: tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON documen
t\n* **Manage a project's clients**: list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from
a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks
to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n
config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename (a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the config token cann
ot detect a concurrent\n one), and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a project's environmen
ts**: list, read, and archive the named\n execution bundles (host + optional server group) that eval\n suites and goals run agai
nst,\n and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project's studies**: name, access mode, attached serv

ers, and
 share link, and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,
 tool-approval policy, and resolved servers
*
**Author eval suites**: create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back;
no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously**: create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` +
`runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appea

r live in the hosted UI,
 tagged `source: "api"`
* **Manage a server's accounts**: complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's
`runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose the default, and dele
te accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn**: send a message history, get back the
\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval suites), and token usage;
the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback**: report a bug, a missing capability, or somethi

ng
 confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls
All endpoint
s operate on servers you have already added to a project in the\nhosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only; see\n[Not in

the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).
## Base URL
```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```\

nThe API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.
## Authentication
Every request needs a
n MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcp
jam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Conte

nt-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```
### Creating a key
1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/setti

ngs/api-keys)
 in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**,
name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately; **it is shown exactly once** and ne

ver
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.
Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immedi

ately.
### Scope
A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. Per-reque
st authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan never reac

h projects outside its organization.
> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot mana
ge API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys

in
> the UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.
### Keep keys secret
Treat an API key like
a password:\n* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager; never commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-s
ide code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement k
ey, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API keys**](https:/
/app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).\nIf you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer
bound to an organization and cannot be used; create a new key\nfrom [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).\n## Conv
entions\n**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads**, the catalog list

ings and eval-run polling, are
`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.
